text: I advice you not to drive in the snow.
why: Note 'a verb with an s' is misleading: with 'I' there is no -s ending; it means the verb is spelled with s (advise vs advice with c). Reword, e.g. 'The verb is spelled with s: advise'.
'gooses' is a real word (3rd person of the informal verb 'to goose'); weaker than tooths/womans as a 'misspelled' prompt. Consider replacing (e.g. 'mouses' -> mice).

text: The shape was the largeest in the room.
why: Corrected sentence 'The shape was the largest in the room' is unnatural (which shape? no comparison set). Use e.g. 'This is the largest room in the house.'

text: Spell the word: the comparative form of dry.
why: Two accepted spellings: 'drier' and 'dryer' (dictionaries list both as comparative of dry). Replace with e.g. happy -> happier.

Correction 'I have never gone abroad' is acceptable but the standard form is 'I have never been abroad'; teaching 'gone' here contradicts the been/gone distinction. Use a sentence where only gone fits, e.g. 'She has went home.' -> 'She has gone home.'

Grammatical, but 'Have you ever been camping?' is the usual form; note 'After have, use gone' is misleading for experience questions (been is also correct). Replace with e.g. 'Where has everybody gone?'

text: My brother has ___ to Spain for a week.
why: No hint: 'been' also fits ('has been to Spain'). Add a hint '(go)' or reword so only gone fits, e.g. 'My brother has ___ to Spain, so he isn't here. (go)'.

text: We ___ for a walk after dinner.
why: No past-time marker or hint: present 'go' (habit) fits as well as 'went'. Add 'Yesterday' / 'last night' and the hint '(go)'.
